Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.37/2024 was registered by Babaleshwar Police Station, Vijayapura against Mayappa Manageni and the petitioners herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of first information received from Srishail Chikkalaki who is the father of deceased Lakshmi.

sentences.text: petitioners who have arrayed as accused Nos.2 and 3 in the FIR were arrested on 17.03.2024.
The bail application filed by them before the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.430/2024 was rejected on 28.03.2024.
Therefore, they are before this Court.
before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the mother and father of accused No.1.
No serious allegations are made against the accused.
More so, against petitioners herein in the first information.

He submits that the deceased had left the matrimonial house earlier and it was the petitioners who had gone to her house and brought her back about a month prior to the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3455 date of incident.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.
He submits that serious allegation of dowry demand and harassment is made against accused.
The marriage of accused No.1 with the deceased was solemnized on 13.03.2023 and within a period of one year from the date of marriage, the death of Lakshmi has taken place.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6. The material on record would go to show that the marriage of accused No.1 who is the son of the petitioners herein with the deceased was solemnized on 13.03.2023.

As per averments made in the first information, prior to the date of marriage, engagement ceremony of accused No.1 with Lakshmi was performed and accused persons allegedly had demanded dowry from the first informant and accordingly 5 thola of gold was given by first informant to the accused persons.
Subsequently, marriage was performed on 13.03.2023.
According to the first informant, even after marriage, his daughter was being harassed in her matrimonial house and demand was made for bringing additional dowry.
Though such allegation is made in the first information, the particular of any such harassment of the accused persons is not found on record.
7. The material on record would go to show that about one year prior to the date of incident Lakshmi had returned to her parents' house and accused No.1 allegedly had quarreled with her in her house.
Subsequently, it is the petitioners who had gone to the parents' house of the deceased Lakshmi and had brought her back to matrimonial house.
On 11.03.2024, Lakshmi consumed poison and had committed suicide.
Though she was shifted to hospital she died while undergoing treatment.
The petitioners are in custody from 17.03.2024.
Major portion of the investigation is already completed.
Accused No.1 is arrested and he is in judicial custody.
The petitioners are NC: 2024:KHC-K:3455 aged persons and they are agriculturist by avocation.
Petitioner No.1 is a lady aged about 50 years and petitioner No.2 is an agriculturist aged about 60 years.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made for grant of regular bail is required to allowed.
8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
